entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -f, --force          Skip the prompt before fetching a remote-only branch
      --trail string   Trail to check out (number, id, or branch; defaults to the current branch's trail)
      --worktree       Check out the trail branch in a worktree under .entire/worktrees instead of switching this checkout

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --repo string    Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; defaults to the origin remote

entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -f, --force          Skip the prompt before fetching a remote-only branch
      --trail string   Trail to check out (number, id, or branch; defaults to the current branch's trail)
      --worktree       Check out the trail branch in a worktree under .entire/worktrees instead of switching this checkout

entire api — Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Current repo: gh/entireio/entire-graph  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

  "body": "Problem:\nThe relation phase of the semantic provider can perform quadratic work when a source file contains deeply nested declarations. For example, 500 nested JavaScript function declarations (approximately 52 KB) require ~37 seconds to process and emit ~386,000 relations, and 1,000 declarations require ~162 seconds. Without a wall-clock ceiling, the indexer has no protection against runaway analysis on pathological inputs. Additionally, the previous implementation made the context non-cancellable during execution, preventing Ctrl-C from terminating a stuck index without killing the entire process.\nSolution:\nWall-clock budget enforcement: Added --max-seconds flag to snapshot, symbols, and edges commands (default: 0 = unlimited). When the deadline expires, the stream is truncated and emits an E_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED partial failure, completes normally with records produced so far, and is not persisted to cache. A complete index of large repositories is unaffected since the budget is opt-in.\nContext deadline handling: The parse and relation phases now use a deadline-based work context instead of context.Background(). A deadline on the caller's context (e.g., from context.WithTimeout) is treated the same as --max-seconds: the snapshot truncates gracefully rather than returning an error.   --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

Examples:
entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)

  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

The critical contract is completeness: a truncated graph must be clearly marked and must never enter a cache as a complete result. Otherwise, Brain could potentially interpret missing symbols as deletions. Preserving schema and stable IDs alone doesn’t protect against that.

My assessment: **broad change, reasonably well validated, suitable for human approval**. The remaining confidence gap is downstream behavior: we did not run an end-to-end Brain reconciliation test against a budget-truncated snapshot. That would be the most valuable additional check if you want stronger assurance.

One header record, then file, external-endpoint, symbol, and relation records.   --include-file <path>   Re-include ignored paths (gitignore-style; not an allowlist)

entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Create the brain:
  add              Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  distill          Distill captured sessions into durable facts (agent-required)
  path             Print the persistent brain path for a repo path or URL
  patterns         Inspect and rebuild repeated-work patterns derived from session history
  refresh          Create or refresh the repository brain
  remember         Author a durable fact about this repository
  status           Summarize the brain: sources, facts, semantic coverage/freshness/blind spots, and live workspace state
  watch            Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)
  workspace        Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces

Explore the brain:
  brief            Build a bounded task packet from brain context and live state
  dash             Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard (status, facts, sessions, history, semantic)
  entities         Query the persisted entity -> checkpoint index (which checkpoints changed a symbol)
  get              Fetch one item in full by id (fact:… | review:… | history:… | conversation:… | conversation-session:… | doc:… | pattern:… | theme:…)
  guide            Print the recommended coding-agent brain command set
  inspect          Run specialist brain inspection commands
  mcp              Serve local brain tools over MCP stdio
  multi-get        Fetch multiple items by id
  overview         Summarize what the project is: stack, boundaries, commands, and recent decisions
  query            Hybrid (lexical+vector, RRF) search across the brain
  recall           Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  search           Lexical keyword search across facts, history, and docs (BM25 for history and docs; token-overlap for facts)
  show             Show one semantic brain record
  verify           Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  viz              Explore the brain as a visual graph in your browser (local, offline)
  vsearch          Vector (semantic) search across facts and docs (history and conversation join with a Gemma-class embedder on the brain_cgo build)

Maintain & share:
  bench            Run local benchmark helpers
  bundle           Import or export local brain bundles
  facts            Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  gc               Prune old local semantic overlays and snapshots
  help             Help about any command
  memory           Inspect and drive the durable conversation-projection work record (hints, jobs, receipts)
  privacy          List, exclude, include, and purge captured sessions from the brain's projections
  publish          Publish the local brain to hosted Entire (opt-in)
  repair           Rebuild local semantic brain derived indexes
  reset            Remove local generated brain data
  stats            Report brain counts and ranges by branch, agent, source, completion state, and index version
  version          Print plugin version

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for entire-brain

Use "entire-brain [command] --help" for more information about a command.

  blame         Show the source anchors a fact was derived from

  context       Build semantic context for a symbol or query
  dead-code     List symbols with no incoming non-structural semantic edges
  graph-schema  Describe the indexed semantic graph schema and relation vocabulary

  ingest-traces Import runtime traces and validate them against static semantic edges
  query-graph   Query semantic graph relations with type:/from:/to: filters
  regressions   Flag suspected regressions by comparing current code to session history
  search-graph  Search semantic graph symbols
  snippet       Return the exact source snippet for an indexed symbol
  tests         Suggest tests relevant to a symbol or query
  trace-path    Find a directed semantic relation path between two symbols

root=Path('/tmp/trail102-e2e')
(root/'REPORT.md').write_text('''# Trail 102 downstream integration check

Tested Graph `b15cabb727bc772be1aae4c711ce0f35b19845b2` against Brain main `c1d9b73ecc087968373cc4477aa41647e82a48d3` using real binaries, a disposable Git repository, and an isolated Brain data directory. Brain was built with `brain_cgo sqlite_fts5`.

## Result

The complete-active-generation preservation check fails. Brain accepts a successful, explicitly budget-truncated Graph stream and promotes its incomplete SQLite generation. It retains the warning and labels retrieval unsafe / low trust. The prior complete generation remains on disk; this test does not demonstrate permanent deletion or deletion tombstones.

| Stage | Symbols | Relations | Sentinel search results | Completeness / trust |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Complete baseline | 75001 | 75001 | 1 | ok / trusted |
| One-second Graph budget | 47900 | 0 | 0 | unsafe / low |
| Unbudgeted recovery | 75001 | 75001 | 1 | ok / trusted |

A subsequent Brain-owned timeout returned an error and preserved the active manifest byte-for-byte. The budgeted Graph cache directory contains zero files. The same fixture commit was used for all three final stages.

## Scope

Brain does not normally request Graph's `--max-seconds`. The supplied `--graph-binary` adapter strips the Entire dispatch prefix and injects `--max-seconds 1` only when `TRAIL102_BUDGET=1`. It uses separate cold cache directories for budgeted and unbudgeted runs. This exercises the requested boundary without synthesizing or altering snapshot records. Brain's usual timeout behavior is a separate, passing control case.

The fixture has 750 Go files with 100 functions each and a final sentinel file. The test invokes `refresh index --force`, the normal explicit replacement path, then queries `inspect search-graph MustSurviveTruncation --json` and inspects the persisted SQLite stores. Counts in budgeted runs are timing-dependent.

## Reproduction in the retained scratch environment

Run from `/tmp/trail102-e2e/fixture`:

```sh
export ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=/tmp/trail102-e2e/data
/tmp/brain-trail102-integration/brain-test refresh index . --force --graph-binary /tmp/trail102-e2e/provider.py
TRAIL102_BUDGET=1 /tmp/brain-trail102-integration/brain-test refresh index . --force --graph-binary /tmp/trail102-e2e/provider.py
PATH=/tmp/trail102-e2e/bin:$PATH /tmp/brain-trail102-integration/brain-test inspect search-graph MustSurviveTruncation --json
# Restore the complete active generation:
/tmp/brain-trail102-integration/brain-test refresh index . --force --graph-binary /tmp/trail102-e2e/provider.py
```

Evidence: `results.json`, `baseline-manifest.json`, `budget-manifest.json`, `recovery-manifest.json`, the corresponding `*-query.json` and logs, plus preserved snapshots and SQLite generations under `data/`.

## Suggested follow-up

Before claiming that a complete active index survives budget truncation, add a Brain-side admission check after merging the final summary and before promoting a generation. Reject `E_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, or require an explicit partial-index policy while preserving the last complete generation. Keep ordinary per-file partial failures distinct from whole-analysis truncation. No production source was modified by this check.
''')
PY

content.text: Okay, but let's say brain has guard, how will it ever get a new snapshot?
Okay, but let's say brain has guard, how will it ever get a new snapshot?

The guard would reject **the incomplete attempt**, not future snapshots.

Brain would keep serving the last complete snapshot, mark it stale, and retry with a larger budget—or without Graph’s optional budget. Once a run completes, Brain switches to the new snapshot. Brain’s own timeout can still stop a hung process.

If the repository consistently takes longer than the allowed budget, retries alone won’t solve it: the budget must increase, indexing must get faster, or the system needs an incremental/resumable protocol.

For this branch, the simplest policy is **keep the last complete generation until a complete replacement arrives**. Partial results could remain available separately, but missing symbols must not imply deletions.

content.text: Ok, but if `--max-seconds` is used, then what?
Ok, but if `--max-seconds` is used, then what?

If `--max-seconds` stays fixed below the time needed to finish, **Brain will never get a complete replacement**. This flag truncates each run; it doesn’t resume where the previous run stopped.

So the caller must choose:

- **Require completeness:** increase/remove the budget, keeping the old snapshot until indexing succeeds.
- **Accept partial coverage:** activate the partial snapshot with explicit warnings, accepting missing search results.

You’re right: a blanket rejection guard would frustrate intentional budgeted indexing. A better Brain policy is to preserve the last complete snapshot while exposing the partial one separately. Combining partial updates safely would require coverage information that distinguishes “processed and deleted” from “never reached.”
